second_order: making, moving, and finding Ladybug marks
theme_note: These codes hold together because people are doing the practical work of putting a recognizable Ladybug-related mark on the canvas and keeping it findable. What varies is the work: proposing an icon, supplying a design and coordinates, shrinking or relocating it, seeking room and help, celebrating completion, and directing others to the finished mark.

second_order: arguing over whose space it is
theme_note: These codes form one exchange in which participants contest who started building first and whether continuing there is rude or a battle. What varies is the move within that dispute: apologizing for toxicity, claiming prior use, offering another place, denying rudeness, and answering sarcastically.

second_order: turning r/place help into crossover threads
theme_note: These codes belong together because participants use contact and help around the canvas to propose continued exchanges between fandoms. What varies is the proposed continuation: thanking helpers, offering newcomer threads, cross-posting reviews, enjoying the crossover, and wishing another fandom were close enough to join it.

second_order: stopping and naming the Hawkmoth CSS joke
theme_note: These codes stay separate because they concern the subreddit's own April Fools styling rather than the canvas: one member tells moderators to stop it and welcomes the restoration, while replies ask what changed and identify the Hawkmoth theme.
